quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #22
										  					
  

18 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: It is against the law for anyone under 21 to ____ alcohol.

options.text: Serve
Wear clothing advertising
Be in the presence of
Transport

questions.explanation: In Pennsylvania, anyone under 21 cannot buy, drink, or carry alcohol. You also cannot have it in your car. Your license can be suspended if you transport alcohol.

questions.question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, you:

options.text: May still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
May no longer turn and must go straight.
Still have the right of way to turn.
Do not have to turn in the arrow's direction anymore.

questions.correctAnswerText: May still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow turns to a solid green light, you can still turn in the arrow's direction. However, you must let pedestrians and oncoming traffic go first.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is false?

options.text: Winter is the most difficult driving season.
You should check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid in winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
Snow tires are best for winter driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or other hazardous conditions. Winter driving is hard and needs extra care. Check your antifreeze and washer fluid regularly. Snow tires help your car grip slippery roads.

questions.question: You may cross solid yellow lines:

options.text: To pass traffic moving the same direction.
Only during daylight hours.
Anytime.
When making turns.

questions.explanation: Broken lines can be crossed, but solid lines cannot. You can only cross solid yellow lines when you are turning.

questions.question: If the rear of your vehicle skids left, you should:

options.text: Steer left.
Use your brakes.
Speed up.
Steer right.

questions.explanation: If your car skids on wet or icy roads, steer in the direction you want to go. If the rear skids left, turn the wheel left. If it skids right, turn the wheel right.

questions.question: Your vehicle is blocking traffic after an accident. You should:

options.text: Move your vehicle off the road if you can.
Never move your vehicle.
Wait for police before moving your vehicle.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle off the road if you can.
questions.explanation: After a minor accident, move your car off the road if possible. Stay at the scene and provide your information.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, turn your front wheels:

options.text: Sharply toward the curb.
Slightly to the right.
Sharply away from the curb.
Straight.

questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply away from the curb when parking uphill. This stops your car from rolling into traffic if your brakes fail.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks with no signals or gates, you should:

options.text: You have the right of way and do not need to check for trains.
You may pass slower drivers while crossing.
Make sure your car fits across the tracks without stopping.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your car fits across the tracks without stopping.
questions.explanation: Check that you have enough room to cross the tracks completely without stopping. Never pass another car at a railroad crossing. Always look for trains before crossing any tracks.

questions.question: To help prevent crashes, you should:

options.text: Signal other drivers and road users.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal other drivers and road users.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do something others do not expect. Signal when you slow down, stop, or turn. Use your horn when needed to warn other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, you should:

options.text: Keep wheels straight and set the parking brake.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply left, away from the curb, when parking uphill. If your brakes fail, your car will not roll into traffic.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow arrow traffic signal?

options.text: Merge into the lane the arrow is pointing to.
Slow down and stop if it is safe to do so.
Turn left after you yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
You have the right-of-way and oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign show?

options.text: Intersection.
Road curve.
Right turn.
Lane change.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection with a crossing road is ahead.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on wet roads?

options.text: Increase your following distance to five or six seconds.
Decrease your following distance to two seconds.
Do not worry about your following distance.
Keep the four-second following distance rule.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance to five or six seconds.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, increase your following distance to five or six seconds.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle yet. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and look to see if the vehicle is on your street.
Slow down but do not stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if the vehicle is on your street.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle, safely pull over to the right and stop until you know it is not coming toward you.

questions.question: What must you do to pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road?

options.text: Do not cross the centerline.
Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.
Use the shoulder.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: To pass on a two-lane, two-way road, you must use the lane for oncoming traffic. Only pass if it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: What do round signs indicate?

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
Upcoming railroad crossings.
Hospitals.

questions.explanation: Round signs warn drivers about an upcoming railroad crossing. Use extra caution when you see this sign.

questions.question: What is a good safety practice when driving through a work zone?

options.text: Drive close to the vehicle in front of you to keep traffic moving.
Reduce your following distance by about half.
Turn on your cruise control.
Double your usual following distance.

questions.explanation: Rear-end collisions are the most common crashes in work zones. Double your following distance in work zones to stay safe.

questions.question: What should car drivers know about large trucks?

options.text: They have large blind spots.
They can stop faster than passenger cars.
They do not need extra room to turn and stop.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Large trucks have blind spots in front, on the sides, and in the back. Stay out of these areas. Trucks also need more space to turn and stop than passenger cars.
